QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_5

question.text: Ganga Infra AIF reports a Kaplan-Schoar PME (KS-PME) of 1.38 against the Nifty 500 TR Index over its fund life. What does this number signify?

answer.text: The AIF underperformed the Nifty 500 TR by 38% in cumulative terms.
The AIF manager is entitled to a 38% catch-up on hurdle.
The AIF has an IRR of 1.38% over the market return.
The AIF outperformed the Nifty 500 TR by 38% on a market-adjusted TVPI basis.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.3.5, KS-PME = (FV of Distributions + NAV) / FV of Capital Calls, where each cash flow is future-valued using the index return to the valuation date. A KS-PME of 1.38 means the AIF's TVPI-equivalent beats the market (if you had invested the same amounts on the same dates in the Nifty 500 TR) by 38%. PME > 1 => outperformance. The Trap: Option A reverses the direction. Option C confuses the multiple (1.38x) with a percentage IRR. Option B confuses it with the distribution waterfall catch-up clause. Note: KS-PME above 1 indicates outperformance versus the listed-market benchmark; the worked example in the workbook gives 1.38 as a market-adjusted TVPI.
